newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev eases on rate cut and ahead of poll.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev eases on rate cut and ahead of poll.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev fell to 1,535-1,545 per dollar at close from the morning's 1,500-1,510 and 1,502-1,506 at the previous close as dollar demand rose on short covering ahead of Saturday's poll, dealers said.

"The lev lost some 35-40 (levs) to the dollar on the day. Banks and clients, including big energy and fuel importers actively bid for dollars for pending payments and short-covering ahead of the elections," a bank dealer said.
Foreign currency supply however was low as traders preferred to close positions ahead of the poll and wait for a cut in the main interest rate to take effect on Monday.

The market was expected to remain cautious next week which could entail a rising pressure on the lev unless the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) countered a further fall in dollar suplly through foreign currency sales, dealers said.

Domestic and foreign investors have opted for high yield lev-denominated instruments since early March as the lev traded stable between 1,500-1,600 and the BNB main interest rate stood between 18 percent and the current 14.15 percent.

The BNB yesterday announced a cut in the main rate to 8.03 percent monthly, in force from Monday, adjusting the rate to the falling yield on short term government securuities auctioned this week. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
